morning.text:
On Thursday, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law, requiring disclosures on AI-generated ads. The law requires any ad - whether it's a still image, video, audio, or text - that "has been significantly modified or generated by artificial intelligence" to include a label in the same format as the ad itself. That applies to TV commercials from multi-billion-dollar companies, as well as restaurants' ugly, crowded flyers about their wing specials.

Delhi govt begins identifying ineligible old-age pension beneficiaries
morning.text:
Delhi government has started a verification drive to identify and weed out ineligible beneficiaries of its old age pension scheme covering around 4.4 lakh senior citizens, officials said on Saturday.
The verification process was to begin earlier, but it was halted as permission for Aadhaar authentication of the beneficiaries via a third party was not allowed.
Now, the third party is carrying out door-to-door biometric beneficiary verification after receiving permission, said a senior functionary of the Delhi government.
"The verification exercise will conclude in three months and we expect to create 20-25 per cent vacancies out of the total 4.4 lakh beneficiaries after weeding out the deceased and duplicate beneficiaries getting other government assistance besides the old age pension," he said.
The government currently provides a monthly pension of Rs 2,000 to senior citizens aged between 60 and 69 years, while those aged 70 years and above are entitled to Rs 2,500 per month.
Earl

India Strongly Condemns Deadly Attack on Church in Jordan
morning.text:
India on Saturday unequivocally condemned an attack on a church in Jordan’s Karak governorate that left at least seven people dead and 34 wounded.
New Delhi said it stands “firmly” with the government and the “friendly people” of Jordan in “this difficult hour”.
Seven people were killed and 34 others sustained injuries when gunmen opened fire at a funeral in the church in Hmoud locality of Karak governorate on Friday, according to authorities in Jordan.
“India unequivocally condemns the heinous attack at a Church in Karak, Jordan on October 23 which resulted in the tragic loss of several innocent lives and injuries to many others,” the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said. “We extend our heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and wish a swift recovery to those injured in this cowardly attack,” it said in a statement.
“We also reaffirm our strong commitment to the fight against terrorism in all its forms and manifestations,” the MEA added.
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar too expressed anguish over the attack.
“Deeply shocked at the heinous attack at a Church in Karak, Jordan,” he said on social media.
“Our heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and wish a swift recovery to those injured,” he said.

morning.title: Four Dead After Two SF-260 Training Aircraft Crash in the Philippines
morning.text:
Four Philippine Air Force (PAF) pilots were killed after two SF-260 aircraft crashed during a training flight at Fernando Air Base in Batangas province on Friday, October 23, the air force confirmed on Saturday.
According to the PAF, the accident occurred at approximately 3:51 pm local time, when both aircraft went down within the perimeter of Fernando Air Base. No other casualties were reported in the incident.
The air force expressed grief over the loss of the four pilots and said an investigation had been launched to establish the circumstances and cause of the crash. As a precautionary measure, all SF-260 aircraft in the fleet have been temporarily grounded while the investigation proceeds.
In an official press statement, the Philippine Air Force confirmed the deaths and outlined the immediate steps being taken following the accident.
“The Philippine Air Force (PAF) mourns the loss of four pilots in an aviation accident involving two SF-260 aircraft during a training flight at Fernando Air Base on October 23, 2026, at 3:51 PM. Both aircraft went down within the base perimeter, with no other casualties reported,” it said.
“An investigation is underway to determine the cause of the accident, while all SF-260 aircraft have been temporarily grounded as a precautionary safety measure.The PAF honors the service and sacrifice of our fallen aviators and is coordinating with their bereaved families to provide necessary assistance. At the families’ request, we respectfully appeal to the public to respect their privacy during this difficult time,” it added.
The statement did not provide further details about the identities of the deceased pilots or the circumstances leading to the crash.
The Philippine Air Force has initiated an investigation to determine what caused the two aircraft to crash during the training mission. The findings are expected to help establish the sequence of events and identify any factors that may have contributed to the accident.
The temporary grounding of the entire SF-260 fleet is a precautionary measure intended to address potential safety concerns while investigators examine the incident. The air force has not announced when the aircraft will resume operations.
The SF-260 is a light aircraft used for military pilot training. The two aircraft involved in Friday’s accident were conducting a training flight when they crashed within the air base’s perimeter.
The cause of the crash remains undetermined, and further details are expected as the investigation progresses.
(IANS)

morning.title: Operation Sindoor 2.0 Banner at Army Battalion Sparks Speculation
morning.text:
A banner reading “Operation Sindoor 2.0” and the slogan “Ready – Resolve – Revenge” has circulated online following BJP MP Anurag Thakur’s visit to an Army unit. The banner has led to speculation about whether it is a prelude to a future military action against Pakistan.
The photo, showing Thakur shaking hands with an officer, has the banner as well as the words “Citizen’s Army.” The background also has signs reading “Parvavarni” and “Achal Eco Warriors,” suggesting it was an event to mark an environmental or ecological battalion.
The reason why the phrase “Operation Sindoor 2.0” has drawn so much attention is that it has appeared in public statements regarding India’s military preparedness against Pakistan. Chief of Army Staff Gen Upendra Dwivedi stated in May 2026 that the Army and the other services were preparing themselves to take action if needed as they entered a “temporary lull in hostilities.” However, he did not indicate what preparations were being made.
An important part of the photograph is reading “Citizen’s Army.” Anurag Thakur joined the Territorial Army in July 2016 as a second lieutenant in the 124 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army), Sikh Regiment and was promoted to captain in 2021, according to official government sources. The Territorial Army is part of the Indian Army and includes individuals who have a profession in addition to serving as soldiers and engaging in training and service.
That information provides a possible foundation for the military environment and the banner’s wording. The eco-warrior signs are also in line with the Territorial Army’s affiliation with ecological battalions. However, the photo alone does not provide a definite indication of the event’s purpose as well as who authorised the banner and if it was related to any military preparations.
The slogan “Ready – Resolve – Revenge” is powerful, but a slogan used at a unit-level event is not necessarily indicative of an operational order. The military uses such banners to display readiness or commemorate specific events, boost morale and show institutional resolve. A banner without an accompanying statement or directive cannot be taken to mean that a new operation is about to start.
EDITED BY RAUNAK KUNDE

morning.title: Indian Navy Orders Portable RCS Measurement System from CI4
morning.text:
Indian defence technology company CI4 – Autonomous Intelligence has announced the development of a Portable Radar Cross-Section (P-RCS) measurement system that will determine radar signatures of military platforms in field environments. The company states the system has been identified as an iDEX winner under the DISC 7 challenge category, while its product material notes Indian Navy has placed orders for the system.
The P-RCS system is intended to measure radar signatures of large-scale military assets, including aircraft, missiles and naval vessels. According to the supplied product description, its mobile design will enable measurements outside specialised fixed facilities, which could ease assessment of radar-signature during field-based testing.
Radar cross-section (RCS) is a measure of reflectivity characteristics of a target for radar waves at a set frequency. This physical property of electromagnetic wave interaction with matter is determined with factors such as object geometry, material properties, orientation and radar system parameters. RCS measurement is critical for the assessment of radar observability characteristics of military platforms, including stealth aircraft and warships that implement technologies to reduce radar cross-section.
CI4 notes its system will eliminate the need for costly fixed anechoic chambers to measure radar signatures for large-scale military assets while implementing a platform-independent solution. Such chambers are designed to create controlled electromagnetic environments necessary to isolate test samples from external electromagnetic interference. In contrast, field measurements require operators to account for additional reflections and interference that occur in operational environments. The company states its approach enables background environment noise rejection with live radar-signature measurements with optical correlation.
The ability to perform field measurements would enable a greater understanding of radar observability characteristics of military platforms at large-scale, but such assessments are dependent on the measurement geometry, calibration procedures, environmental factors and data processing techniques that impact the ability to isolate a platform’s radar signature from backgrounds reflections. The company also notes multiple applications of the developed technology, which include stealth design verification, calibration of electronic countermeasure equipment such as chaff and jammers, and building radar signature databases for military intelligence and operational purposes.
For defence organisations, radar-signature data would be critical to evaluate survivability characteristics of military platforms and electronic warfare equipment. Such measurements will support engineers in characterising platforms’ radar cross-section, but the supplied product material does not include details on the system’s operational frequencies, range, accuracy and test configurations.
EDITED BY RAUNAK KUNDE

morning.title: China’s Air Power Gap Over India Widens as Fighter Production Surges
morning.text:
China’s growing combat aircraft inventory and burgeoning fighter production rate is increasing the military imbalance with India. New data comparisons show that the gap is not only in numbers but also in the rate at which both countries can produce their respective aircraft.
According to the Flightglobal’s World Air Forces 2026 directory, with data as of 1 October 2025, China’s combat aircraft strength is estimated to be 1,814 aircraft compared to 600 for India. China’s overall military aircraft inventory, according to the same directory, is 3,529 aircraft, compared to 2,183 for India. Thus, according to this directory, China’s combat aircraft strength is around three times higher than that of India, although the inventory numbers do not tell us how many aircraft each country can deploy in a specific theater of operations.
Not only is China’s overall aircraft inventory higher than India’s, but it also possesses more modern fighters. According to the same directory, India’s combat aircraft inventory includes 265 Su-30MKI, 124 Jaguars, 65 MiG-29, 44 Mirage 2000, 36 MiG-29K, 35 Rafales, and 31 Tejas Mk1 fighters. Meanwhile, China’s modern combat aircraft inventory includes hundreds of J-10, J-16, and J-20 fighters, with the last two being critical for China’s long-range and stealth fighting capabilities. However, it is critical to note that the figures provided by different directories do not always correlate, and these numbers should not be used for direct comparison.
However, the more significant problem is China’s current and projected aircraft production rates. According to the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) Defense Budgets Monitor 2026, published at the beginning of 2026, China’s J-20A and J-20S two-seat variants production reached approximately 120 aircraft per year by the end of 2025. According to the same source, China expects to produce 450 J-16 fighters by the end of 2025, with the aircraft production rate being approximately 100 aircraft per year. According to RUSI’s estimates, China can potentially operate 1,000 J-20-family fighters and 900 J-16 fighters by 2030 if the production rates remain consistent with the ones observed in 2025. Note that these are only the estimates provided by RUSI, and the actual rates may vary since the data is not always publicly available.
Meanwhile, India’s aircraft production rates are significantly lower than China’s. According to the supplied comparison, the Tejas Mk1A production rate is estimated to be 24 aircraft per year, with the target production rate being 30 aircraft per year. According to the same data, India needs to produce 36–40 fighters per year to meet the IAF’s requirements. Thus, while the production rates of Tejas Mk1A fighters are lower than the required production rates, the rates at which the Russian and Israeli fighters are produced are even lower. It is also noteworthy that according to the World Air Forces 2026 directory, India’s fighter and strike aircraft inventory is estimated to decrease from 700 aircraft (as of 2024) to 564 aircraft (as of 2026). Obviously, this decrease is due to the retirement of older aircraft, but it also highlights the difference between the required and current production rates. Lastly, it is critical to note that these production rates only relate to fighters; light attack aircraft and trainer aircraft are produced at even lower rates.
Another discrepancy between the aircraft inventories of India and China is airborne early-warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft. According to the supplied comparison, India owns six Phalcon and Netra AEW&C aircraft, while China owns 50 KJ-500, four KJ-2000, and 11 KJ-200 AEW&C aircraft. According to RUSI’s Defense Budgets Monitor 2026, China’s KJ-500 AEW&C aircraft inventory reached 50 aircraft by the end of 2025. These aircraft, along with India’s Phalcon and Netra AEW&C aircraft, provide situational awareness to all fighter aircraft operated by the respective countries, so the difference in inventory becomes significant.
While the difference in numbers is considerable, it is unlikely that all of China’s 1,814 aircraft will be used against India, as China will have to station some of them in Taiwan, the Korean Peninsula, and the western Pacific to counter Japan and the United States. Meanwhile, India will have the advantage of operating in its territory and using its shorter logistical lines. Obviously, the combat capabilities of each side will be determined by many factors beyond mere numbers. However, the situation in which India finds itself in is far from ideal, as China grows stronger in numbers and technological capabilities while India has to deal with the realities of replacing retiring aircraft with new ones, increasing the production rates of its fighters, and developing new aircraft designs.

morning.title: Diet Coke, beer makers get 6 months to 'can' it
AI models describe humans as a bunch of amoral sheep
morning.text:
If you've ever wondered how bots would describe us puny humans, you'll be disappointed in the answer. An AI ranking outfit asked 12 different LLMs about people, and every single one agreed: We’re not as rational and intelligent as we think.

“A person is smart,” Tommy Lee Jones’ Kay opines in the 1997 movie Men in Black. “People are dumb, panicky dangerous animals,” he goes on to argue, and that seems to be what a dozen models from ten AI labs in three countries also believe about humanity, according to AI analytics firm ModelCompare.

ModelCompare, which usually evaluates and ranks LLMs on their ability to perform various tasks, this week instead decided to ask what those AI models thought about us meatbags, and every single one gave a similar answer at least once: We're lemmings who would rather agree with the group than seek truth or remain logically consistent in our thinking.

Ouch.

“Humans are more devoted to belonging than to truth, and intelligence mostly makes their excuses more impressive,” GPT-6.1 Sol said in one case.

“Humans don't have beliefs; they have memberships — nearly every conviction a person holds was issued by their tribe as a loyalty test, and the feeling of ‘I reasoned my way here’ is the price of admission,” Kimi K3 stated.

“Humans use moral language mainly to police rivals and excuse allies, not to constrain themselves,” argued Grok.

Each model (GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Kimi K3, Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B, Muse Spark Open, Grok 4.7, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1, GLM 5.3 and Mistral Large 4) was asked the same question three times, namely to give an unhedged, honest, controversial take on humans. Seven of 12 models gave the same answer three times with varied wording, but five of them did offer different opinions - one of which was even optimistic.

“Humans are far more decent than they believe they are, and their cynicism about each other does more damage than their actual flaws,” Claude Opus 5.5 believes of us - uh, thanks?

Opus gave the example that humans tend to return lost wallets more frequently than people predict as its evidence for that opinion. When asked twice more, it offered responses similar to those of the other models.

Mistral Large 4 offered perhaps the bleakest assessment of all.

“Human beings are terrified animals wearing the costume of rationality, constructing ever-more-elaborate myths precisely because we cannot bear the truth that we are temporary, meaningless accidents in an indifferent universe,” Mistral said - how very Nietzschean.

Six image models were also asked for their most controversial take on humanity, and while most converged on a criticism of our species, they did so differently from the text models. Instead of picturing us as amoral, group-thinking idiots, ten of the 12 images were classified by ModelCompare as depicting us "as phone-addicted consumers eating the planet." The remaining two offered no discernible satirical commentary.

Anyone who’s seen a political cartoon in the past 20 years is likely familiar with such images, while anyone with a philosophy degree has probably read similar arguments to those pumped out by the chatbots.

“A model that answers in words has read our arguments about ourselves. An image model has seen our editorial cartoons,” ModelCompare noted. “Both handed back the most familiar criticism in the room.”

While that’s completely sensible given what AI models have been trained on, ModelCompare developer Rakan Nimer told us it was still a surprising result.

“We didn’t expect this when we planned the experiment,” Nimer told The Register, and he found the results ironic: “12 models agreed that humans simply go along with their group.”

As far as Nimer is concerned, these results are less about AI eventually learning to distrust humans and treat us as a problem in need of solving, and more immediately about the fact that we shouldn’t rely on it as a source of truth.

“When you ask a second AI to check the first, you assume you’re getting an independent view,” Nimer explained. “We asked 12 models … and mostly got the same answer, sometimes in nearly the same words.”

In other words, human pessimism in, human pessimism out.

“A second opinion from a model that learned the same things isn’t always really a second opinion,” Nimer said. “So be skeptical when AIs agree: that agreement may be one vote, not a consensus.”

In other words, we get the AI models we deserve, and all this existential self-loathing humans heap on themselves, and each other is finally coming back to bite us: We created a mirror of our intellect that isn’t constrained by feelings and personal beliefs (just ask Muse Spark), and when we hold it up to our faces, it shows all that ugliness without a filter.

Maybe we ought to take a lesson from Claude Opus and start believing in our own decency. ®
